title: Vesper and the Room
premise: Ansel Ashgrove, a property surveyor, returns to her late grandmother's house to appraise it for sale and finds every old photograph now contains an extra chair that no one remembers buying. The house has been keeping a tenant: something her grandmother invited in decades ago in exchange for the family's survival during a desperate winter, a bargain renewed each time the well refills. As night falls, Ansel must choose between completing the appraisal and letting the thing pass to the next owner, or destroying the deed and confronting it herself. She survives until sunrise by offering the one payment the entity cannot refuse—the truth spoken aloud—and ends the cycle, though the chair follows her home.
about_author: Orsen Almeida is the pen name of a former rural assessor who spent years cataloguing houses no one wanted to enter twice. They write horror about paperwork, inheritance, and the small legal fictions that keep terrible things at bay.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Arriving to appraise the house, she catalogs rooms with professional detachment until she notices the extra chair appearing in decades of family photographs—always empty, always closer to the camera. The emotional beat is denial curdling into dread as her rational explanations run out and she realizes the house has been waiting for her specifically.

chapters.title: What Grandma Signed
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, intercut with grandmother's 1974 letters found in the attic. She learns of the winter bargain: survival traded for tenancy, renewed whenever the well refills. The emotional beat is grief reframed as complicity—her beloved grandmother was both victim and keeper, and Ansel inherits the debt along with the deed.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV through the night. The entity manifests fully, testing her with visions of everyone she failed to save, offering escape if she simply signs the appraisal and walks away. The emotional beat is terror giving way to fury as she understands staying invisible was always how it fed—on silence, on unspoken truths.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV at dawn. She burns the deed and speaks the whole truth aloud—naming the bargain, the deaths, her own years of willful blindness—breaking the contract's power over secrecy. The emotional beat is exhausted, costly victory: justice outside any law, love finally outweighing duty, shadowed by the chair now sitting in her own apartment.
